touches.text: The abstract ticket owns what every kind shares: its birth (cast) and its three parts, each with one job: the plan (only what a builder builds from), the metadata and state (what gates and doors read and write as it moves), and the history (the append-only log). WHY: one job per part reduces confusion; a builder reads the plan and nothing else.
Coding Ticket: what we usually mean.
Has its own workflow stamped on it (the state string, with the cursor). Each workflow step declares what it needs.
Lives in CairnCommons/tickets/ while staged; its trail migrates beside its code as that component's history while under way, and back to the commons after (Law 5).
Owns the inspectors and gates (9.4): everything in the code pipeline that checks. The exception is diagnostic_inspector, which is base's (17.1).

Outline check: when a ticket is cast, the cheapest model reads it beside the outline sections it touches. A conflict, or an open question in those sections, becomes a question on the ticket, which holds its build until answered. It reads the outline as it stands each time, so editing the outline costs nothing. [Q#96: A ticket-v2 decision line carries n, text and by on every line (census 2026-09-16: 70 of 70), and by is free prose, so nothing checks it. The cast door (the shaped plan) already refuses a line with no writes_to or reads.
